review_notes: I read the whole file and the Core.lean and SparseFiniteFamily.lean simp setup. I also grepped the repo for uses of sparseNormalizedFamily and the membership lemmas. The core eval_eq_true lemmas for Clause and CNF are already @[simp], so the file's simp-only proofs depend on them. I found no rewrite loops or competing rules. I only weakly considered making the eval-of-toList lemmas simp. Their only use is a direct .trans, so I did not report them. I did not run Lean, so the proposed simp attribute is untested.

findings.excerpt:
theorem mem_sparseNormalizedFamily {H : CNF V} {C : Clause V} :
    C ∈ sparseNormalizedFamily H ↔ C ∈ H ∧ C.Normalized := by
  classical
  simp [sparseNormalizedFamily]
findings.problem: sparseNormalizedFamily is defined as `by classical exact H.toFinset.filter Clause.Normalized`, so it is only reachable through this membership lemma. The lemma is not tagged @[simp]. Downstream proofs therefore cannot let simp reduce `C ∈ sparseNormalizedFamily H`. In sparseNormalizedFamily_eval, `simp only [CNF.eval_eq_true, Finset.mem_toList]` leaves the goal `C ∈ sparseNormalizedFamily H`, and the proof then applies `.mpr` and `.mp` by hand. sparseNormalizeOfNoEmpty repeats the pattern `(mem_sparseNormalizedFamily.mp (sparseMinimalFamily_subset _ hC)).1` and `.2` three times. The result is verbose manual projections and a more fragile interface. A client has to know to unfold the private-looking definition or to cite the lemma by name.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp] theorem mem_sparseNormalizedFamily`. This is safe: the right-hand side `C ∈ H ∧ C.Normalized` mentions no sparseNormalizedFamily, so the rule terminates and is the canonical unfolding of membership. It matches how Finset.mem_filter is a simp lemma. Then `simp only [CNF.eval_eq_true, Finset.mem_toList, mem_sparseNormalizedFamily]` would turn the eval_eq proof into a plain forall/and goal, shortening sparseNormalizedFamily_eval. Use `simp only [mem_sparseMinimalFamily, mem_sparseNormalizedFamily]` for the field proofs of sparseNormalizeOfNoEmpty. The same attribute is also missing on the companion `mem_sparseMinimalFamily` in SparseFiniteFamily.lean.
findings.benefit: Membership in the normalized family reduces automatically to the intended normal form `C ∈ H ∧ C.Normalized`. This removes the repeated manual `.mp`/`.mpr` projections in this file and makes the family usable from simp in later files without exposing its `classical` filter definition.
